title: Rules become hooks
source: ai-os docs/rules-hooks/PLAN.md and PLAN-summary.md, merged by thread D (commit 9d32f085).

beats.say: Right now, every agent reads about seventeen thousand words of rules before it starts. ... That's too much, so many get skipped. ... The plan cuts that to about fifty-five lines, and the rest shows up only at the moment it's needed.

slide.label: Rules into hooks
slide.title: From *17,000 words* to 55 lines
slide.lede: A small core every agent reads. Everything else arrives at the exact moment it matters.
slide.total: Six choices you might want to veto.

beats.say: First, details files. ... Agents will write one only when a reply runs long. ... Readthroughs and reels, like this one, happen only when you ask. ... Second, one simple act or wait rule replaces ten. ... Pushes to main stop asking you, except the crossword.

items.head: Details files only for long replies
items.sub: Readthroughs and reels only when you ask

items.head: One act-or-wait rule replaces ten
items.sub: Pushes to main stop asking, except the crossword

beats.say: Third, the four design steps become one. ... You see three real examples, you pick one, and then it gets built. ... Fourth, learning happens once a week, not every turn, and brings you at most three rule changes.

items.head: Three examples, you pick, it's built
Learning runs once a week
items.sub: At most three rule changes for you to OK

beats.say: Fifth, if an agent wants to edit anything in your school folders, it asks you first. ... That protects your coursework.

slide.label: Veto five
slide.title: School folders are *guarded*
items: Agents ask before editing school files

beats.say: Sixth, beta rules. ... Agents can write their own small rules and run them without your OK. ... But they can only add reminders, never override a real rule. ... They're tagged, there are five at most, and each one expires in three weeks unless you promote it.

items.head: Only adds reminders
items.sub: Can never override an official rule

items.head: Tagged and capped at five
items.sub: You can always see which are running

beats.say: Two more things were added. ... A rules dashboard on your Mac shows what each rule does, with on and off switches in your Tweaks panel. ... And coordinators now send big questions to an advisor before acting on them.

items.head: Local rules dashboard
items.sub: Switches live in your Tweaks panel

items.head: Big asks go to an advisor first

beats.say: What comes first? ... The fixes that cost you the most. ... The school guard, and a check at the end of each turn so agents stop asking for OKs they don't need. ... Rules agents already follow, like using bun, come later.

slide.label: What comes first
slide.title: Biggest pain, *fixed first*
slide.total: If none of the six bother you, it goes ahead.
